description.value: This study examined the effects of standard 12-month dialectical behavior therapy on emotion regulation and amygdala activity in unmedicated patients with borderline personality disorder, compared with healthy controls.

value: We hypothesized that the BPD patients would show a decrease in amygdala reactivity following treatment, and that the magnitude of this change would be associated with improved emotion regulation as measured by the DERS.

We hypothesized that the HC group would show consistent amygdala activation over time and their emotion regulation scores on the DERS would also remain stable over time (i.e. baseline, 6 months, 12 months).
